edits.html:
Eyelid Lumps and Swelling in a Child

Tender nodule on the lid margin with a red eye and no fever · NBME · where is the swelling, and does it spread beyond the lump?

Source vignette Pt — 10 yo M, 2 days of redness and mild pain in the left eye; afebrile · Exam — left conjunctiva mildly red, swollen and tender; a 3-mm nodule on the lower lid margin, toward the outer corner; right eye normal · Q — the most appropriate treatment; options spanned nasolacrimal massage, oral amoxicillin, topical prednisolone, topical tetrahydrozoline and warm compresses
The decision point

A tender nodule on the eyelid margin, with local redness and no fever, is a hordeolum (stye). It is an acute infection of an eyelid gland, usually by Staphylococcus aureus. First-line treatment is warm compresses with gentle lid massage several times a day. Heat softens the blocked gland contents so the gland can drain. Conjunctival redness and swelling beside the nodule come from surface irritation and do not make this conjunctivitis.

Add oral antibiotics only when redness and swelling spread across the lid, which is preseptal cellulitis. A lesion that has not settled after several weeks of compresses goes to ophthalmology for incision and drainage.

Lump or swelling of the eyelid in a child: the differential
DiagnosisBrief illness scriptKey discriminatorWhy less likely here
Hordeolum (stye)Acute staphylococcal infection of a lash follicle or eyelid gland; warm compresses and lid massageTender, red nodule on the lid margin, sometimes with a yellow pointFits: 2 days, tender 3-mm nodule on the margin, afebrile
ChalazionSterile, chronic inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland, sometimes left behind by a hordeolum; compresses, then steroid injection or incision if it persistsPainless, firm nodule in the body of the lid, away from the margin, present for weeksThis nodule is tender, on the margin and 2 days old
DacryocystitisInfection of the lacrimal sac behind a blocked nasolacrimal duct; oral antibiotics, with warm compresses as supportTender swelling at the inner corner of the eye, beside the nose; pus from the punctum on pressureThe nodule sits on the lid margin toward the outer corner
Preseptal cellulitisInfection of the lid in front of the orbital septum, from a skin break, hordeolum or dacryocystitis; oral amoxicillin-clavulanateDiffuse red, warm, swollen lid; eye movements and vision normal, no proptosisRedness and swelling stay at the nodule, and there is no fever
Orbital cellulitis Can't missInfection behind the septum, usually spread from ethmoid sinusitis; computed tomography of the orbits with contrast and intravenous antibioticsProptosis, pain with eye movement, limited eye movement or reduced visionNone of these is described, and he is afebrile
BlepharitisChronic inflammation of both lid margins, often with seborrheic dermatitis; lid hygiene and warm compressesBoth lids red and crusted along the lash line, worse on waking, with no discrete noduleOne focal nodule in one eye
Management ladder: the tender lid nodule
TierInterventionEscalate when
1. HordeolumWarm compresses several times a day with gentle lid massage; do not squeeze the lesionRedness and swelling spread across the lid; or no improvement after several weeks, when ophthalmology offers incision and drainage
2. Preseptal cellulitisOral antibiotic covering Staphylococcus aureus and streptococci, such as amoxicillin-clavulanate, with close follow-upProptosis, pain with eye movement, limited eye movement or reduced vision; or worsening on oral antibiotics
3. Orbital cellulitisAdmission, computed tomography of the orbits with contrast, intravenous antibiotics and ophthalmology consultationAbscess on imaging or falling vision: surgical drainage
Scenario bank
Pearls Squeezing a hordeolum can spread the infection into the lid · A lump at the inner corner of the eye is the lacrimal sac, not an eyelid gland · Topical steroid drops treat anterior uveitis and are avoided when infection is possible
How NBME framed it The stem opened with a red, sore eye and conjunctival swelling, and it described the lump on the lid margin without ever naming a stye. Each wrong option was the right treatment for a neighboring eye problem: a blocked tear duct, preseptal cellulitis, uveitis or simple redness.
Pairs with Part I The Red Eye covers conjunctivitis and the can't-miss red eyes, including uveitis, where topical steroids belong. Ask: does the redness come from the conjunctiva, or from a lump on the lid? Part I Sinusitis with Intracranial Extension covers preseptal versus orbital cellulitis and orbital imaging. Ask: are eye movements painful or limited, and is there proptosis?
Transferable rule Locate the swelling before treating it. A tender nodule on the lid margin gets warm compresses. Antibiotics start when redness spreads across the lid, and imaging when the eye protrudes or eye movement hurts.
Unchecked attributeNasolacrimal massage: it sounds like the lid massage that goes with compresses; it treats a blocked tear duct at the inner corner, and this nodule is on the lid margin toward the outer corner.
Sequencing trapOral amoxicillin: the nodule is an infection; there is no fever and no redness spreading across the lid, so there is no cellulitis to treat.
True-fact-wrong-slotTopical prednisolone: the eye is inflamed; steroid drops treat anterior uveitis, and a tender lump on the lid margin is not uveitis; steroids are also avoided when infection is possible.
Salient decoyTopical tetrahydrozoline: it clears the redness the stem opens with; this vasoconstrictor acts at alpha-1 and alpha-2 receptors and does nothing for the blocked gland.

edits.companion: hordeolum; heat helps the blocked gland drain
edits.lead_in: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

edits.stem: 8 yo F with a painless, rubbery 6-mm nodule in the middle of the upper eyelid, away from the margin; it began as a tender red bump 2 months ago and has not shrunk despite warm compresses; no redness, discharge or fever
edits.answer: Ophthalmology referral for incision and curettage
edits.companion: chalazion; an intralesional steroid injection is the alternative

edits.stem: 4 yo F with 2 days of a tender, red swelling just below the inner corner of the right eye, beside the nose; pressing on it brings pus from the lower punctum; afebrile; eye movements full and vision normal
edits.companion: acute dacryocystitis; probing waits until the infection settles

edits.stem: 6 yo M with a stye on the left upper lid 4 days ago, now with diffuse redness, warmth and swelling of both left lids; T 38.2 C; vision normal, eye movements full and painless, no proptosis
edits.answer: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and close outpatient follow-up
edits.companion: preseptal cellulitis spreading from a hordeolum
edits.d1: Warm compresses and lid massage alone
edits.d2: Computed tomography of the orbits and intravenous antibiotics

edits.stem: 12 yo F with 1 day of a tender, red nodule with a yellow point on the upper lid margin; afebrile; no redness beyond the nodule
edits.answer: Squeezing the nodule to express the pus
edits.companion: squeezing can spread the infection into the lid
edits.d1: Warm compresses several times a day
edits.d2: Gentle lid massage after each compress
edits.lead_in: Which of the following should be avoided?

edits.stem: 11 yo M with months of burning, itchy eyes that are worse on waking; both lid margins are red and crusted, with flakes on the lashes and no discrete nodule; scaly patches on the scalp

edits.html: Pairs with Part II Eyelid Lumps and Swelling in a Child covers the red eye that comes from a tender lump on the lid margin, and its lid-swelling mimics. Ask: is there a lump on the lid?
Pairs with Part II Eyelid Lumps and Swelling in a Child covers the hordeolum and dacryocystitis that can spread into preseptal cellulitis. Ask: is the swelling a focal lump or the whole lid?
